claim: Hippocampal neurons were prepared from E17.5 rat embryos and cultured in neurobasal medium supplemented with Gem21 NeuroPlex.
source: Hippocampal neurons were prepared from E17.5 rat embryos as previously described (Dotti et al., 1988), and were cultured in neurobasal medium supplemented with Gem21 NeuroPlex (GEMINI bio-products, West Sacramento, CA).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the preparation and culture conditions of hippocampal neurons, citing a previous protocol.

claim: Culturing hippocampal cells isolated from embryonic day 17.5 rat brain on compliant gels can selectively enrich the population of neurons by up to 80% and minimize growth of glial cells.
source: Culturing hippocampal cells isolated from embryonic day 17.5 (E17.5) rat brain on these compliant gels can selectively enrich the population of neurons by up to 80% and minimize growth of glial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E showing cell type enrichment analysis.

claim: Upon initial gel contact, cells formed a uniform lamellipodial extension.
source: Upon initial gel contact, cells formed a uniform lamellipodial extension (Figure 1A1, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B)
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy images showing lamellipodial extensions in the referenced figures.

claim: Lamellipodia are well-known morphological precursors of neurites.
source: Lamellipodia are well-known morphological precursors of neurites (Figure 1—figure supplement 2; Dehmelt et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous literature and supplementary figure data.

claim: Neurites formed only if their preceding lamellipodia occupied less than a third of the entire cell periphery.
source: However, we observed that neurites formed only if their preceding lamellipodia occupied less than a third of the entire cell periphery; lamellipodia occupying >1/3 of the periphery failed to form neurites even at the 16 hr time-point (Figure 1A2–A4, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of lamellipodium occupancy and neurite formation shown in the referenced figures.

claim: In 5 hr soft-gel cultures (0.1 kPa), nearly 100% of cells formed segmented lamellipodia.
source: For example, in 5-hr soft-gel cultures (0.1 kPa), nearly 100% of cells formed SL (Figure 1A4, A5, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data presented in the referenced figures showing the percentage of cells with segmented lamellipodia.

claim: Most cells (~71.5%) on stiff-gel cultures (E = 20 kPa) or coverslips (glass) failed to form segmented lamellipodia and instead formed a single broad lamellipodium.
source: whereas most cells (~71.5%) on stiff-gel cultures (E = 20 kPa) or coverslips (glass) failed to form SL and instead formed a single BL (Figure 1A4, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data showing the distribution of lamellipodium phenotypes on different substrate stiffnesses.

claim: In 16 hr cultures, the segmented lamellipodia of most (~98%) cells on soft gels had become neurites.
source: In 16 hr cultures, the SL of most (~98%) cells on soft gels had become neurites, whereas more than half (~57.3%) of the cells on stiff gels possessed BL and lacked neurites (Figure 1A5).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of neurite formation at 16 hours shown in Figure 1A5.

claim: Culturing cells on environments with elastic moduli <1 kPa, which match the mechanical properties of brain (E = 0.1—1 kPa), is sufficient to initiate neurite formation.
source: The fact that cells form neurites on soft gels in the absence of neurite-promoting growth factors suggests that culturing cells on environments with elastic moduli <1 kPa, which match the mechanical properties of brain (E = 0.1—1 kPa; (Christ et al., 2010; Georges et al., 2006), is sufficient to initiate neurite formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations and citations to literature on brain mechanical properties.

claim: Using mRNA microarray and Gene Ontology analyses, 114 differentially expressed mRNA transcripts were identified in cells grown on 0.1 kPa and 20 kPa gels at the 5 hr time-point.
source: Using mRNA microarray and Gene Ontology analyses, we identified 114 differentially expressed mRNA transcripts in cells grown on 0.1 kPa and 20 kPa gels at the 5 hr time-point (filtering criteria: fold change ≥1.5, p<0.05; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, and Appendix 1—table 1, 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by microarray data analysis with specific filtering criteria and presented in supplementary figures and tables.

claim: Three genes—Cltc, Dab2, and Myo6, all of which function in clathrin-mediated endocytosis—were co-upregulated in 0.1 kPa gel cultures at the 5 hr time-point.
source: Notably, three genes—Cltc, Dab2, and Myo6, all of which function in clathrin-mediated endocytosis—were co-upregulated in 0.1 kPa gel cultures at the 5 hr time-point (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by microarray data validated by QuantiGene Plex assay shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Several adhesion factors, including Vcl, Nrcam, Robo2 and Cdh11, were relatively upregulated in 20 kPa gel cultures at 5 hr and/or 16 hr compared to cells grown on softer substrates.
source: By contrast, several adhesion factors, including Vcl, Nrcam, Robo2 and Cdh11, were relatively upregulated in 20 kPa gel cultures at 5 hr and/or 16 hr compared to cells grown on softer substrates (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Segmented lamellipodium cells expressed relatively lower (2.3- to 10-fold) levels of adhesion-related mRNA compared to broad lamellipodium cells.
source: In 5 hr cultures, we found that SL cells expressed relatively lower (2.3- to 10-fold) and higher (1.2- to 4-fold) levels of adhesion-related (Vcl, Cdh11 and Robo2) and endocytic (Cltc, Dab2, and Myo6) mRNA, respectively, compared to those of BL cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by single molecule RNA FISH data quantifying mRNA levels in different cell phenotypes.

claim: Segmented lamellipodium cells expressed relatively higher (1.2- to 4-fold) levels of endocytic mRNA compared to broad lamellipodium cells.
source: In 5 hr cultures, we found that SL cells expressed relatively lower (2.3- to 10-fold) and higher (1.2- to 4-fold) levels of adhesion-related (Vcl, Cdh11 and Robo2) and endocytic (Cltc, Dab2, and Myo6) mRNA, respectively, compared to those of BL cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by single molecule RNA FISH data quantifying mRNA levels in different cell phenotypes.

claim: Cells grown on 0.1 kPa gels exhibited a ~1.6-fold greater FM4-64 intensity at the end-point of the measurements (t = 40 min) compared to cells grown on 20 kPa gels.
source: We observed that cells grown on 0.1 kPa gels exhibited a ~1.6-fold greater FM4-64 intensity at the end-point of the measurements (t = 40 min), and a ~1.7-fold greater uptake rate [t½ (0.1 kPa) v.s. t½ (20 kPa)=16.8 min v.s. 24.8 min] than cells grown on 20 kPa gels (Figure 1B1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative FM4-64 uptake measurements shown in Figure 1B1.

claim: Cells grown on 0.1 kPa gels exhibited a ~1.7-fold greater FM4-64 uptake rate than cells grown on 20 kPa gels.
source: We observed that cells grown on 0.1 kPa gels exhibited a ~1.6-fold greater FM4-64 intensity at the end-point of the measurements (t = 40 min), and a ~1.7-fold greater uptake rate [t½ (0.1 kPa) v.s. t½ (20 kPa)=16.8 min v.s. 24.8 min] than cells grown on 20 kPa gels (Figure 1B1).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of FM4-64 uptake kinetics shown in Figure 1B1.

claim: Robust dye uptake was pharmacologically and genetically abolished by applying inhibitors of dynamin GTPase and by ectopically expressing a dominant-negative Dynamin II mutant (DynIIK44A).
source: Robust dye uptake was pharmacologically and genetically abolished by applying inhibitors of dynamin GTPase and by ectopically expressing a dominant-negative Dynamin II mutant (DynIIK44A; (Damke et al., 1994; Herskovits et al., 1993) in 0.1 kPa cultures, respectively (Figure 1B1, B2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using pharmacological inhibitors and genetic manipulation shown in Figures 1B1 and 1B2.

claim: An average invagination rate of ~7 QD-BDNF dots per cell was observed in 0.1 kPa cultures over the first 5 hr after bath application.
source: We observed an average invagination rate of ~7 dots per cell in 0.1 kPa cultures over the first 5 hr after bath application of QD-BDNF. That rate was significantly decreased to two dots per cell in 20 kPa cultures (Figure 1B3)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements of QD-BDNF internalization shown in Figure 1B3.

claim: The QD-BDNF invagination rate was significantly decreased to two dots per cell in 20 kPa cultures.
source: We observed an average invagination rate of ~7 dots per cell in 0.1 kPa cultures over the first 5 hr after bath application of QD-BDNF. That rate was significantly decreased to two dots per cell in 20 kPa cultures (Figure 1B3)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements of QD-BDNF internalization shown in Figure 1B3.

claim: Nearly all (~100%) control cortical neurons exhibited a neurite-bearing, polarized morphology.
source: Nearly all (~100%) control cortical neurons (i.e. those solely expressing marker protein) exhibited a neurite-bearing, polarized morphology (Figure 1C1, C3), with dendritic arbors being oriented toward the pial surface and the axon being oriented radially in the cortical plate.
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological analysis of control neurons in vivo shown in Figures 1C1 and 1C3.

claim: Cortical neurons expressing DynIIK44A exhibited an apparent migration defect.
source: By contrast, cortical neurons expressing DynIIK44A exhibited an apparent migration defect (Figure 1C1, C2), with a high percentage of cells having a non-polarized morphology without extension of minor processes (termed 'no neurite') and a reduced percentage of cells exhibiting a polarized morphology (unipolar or bipolar) (Figure 1C3).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo analysis of neurons expressing DynIIK44A shown in Figures 1C1, 1C2, and 1C3.

claim: A normal level of endocytic reactions is required for proper neurite formation and radial migration of newly generated cortical neurons.
source: Thus, a normal level of endocytic reactions is required for proper neurite formation and radial migration of newly generated cortical neurons; two tightly linked events during neuronal development in vivo.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that inhibition of endocytosis impairs neurite formation and migration.

claim: Rac1 activity decreased with increasing stiffness of the substrate in 5 hr neuronal cultures.
source: Using an active Rac1 pulldown assay, immunofluorescent staining of Rac1 or active Rac1, and the FRET biosensor Rac1-2G (Fritz et al., 2013; Fritz et al., 2015), we observed that, unlike RhoA, Rac1 activity decreased with increasing stiffness of the substrate in 5 hr neuronal cultures (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple assays measuring Rac1 activity shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Active Rac1 accumulated in segmented lamellipodia and the tips of growing neurites, whereas there was no accumulation in broad lamellipodia.
source: In addition, active Rac1 accumulated in SL and the tips of growing neurites, whereas there was no accumulation in BL (Figure 2A1, A3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging of active Rac1 shown in Figures 2A1 and 2A3.

claim: Either expression of DynIIK44A or treatment with inhibitors of endocytosis significantly blocked accumulation of active Rac1.
source: Consistently, ratiometric FRET imaging confirmed accumulation of active Rac1 at segmented neuronal lamellipodia on soft gels (0.1 kPa), with FRET signal decreasing from the leading edge to the cell body (Figure 2B1, B2). Moreover, either expression of DynIIK44A or treatment of the 0.1 kPa cultures with inhibitors of endocytosis significantly blocked accumulation of active Rac1 (Figure 2A1–A3).
evidence: The claim is supported by FRET imaging and immunofluorescence data showing that endocytosis inhibition blocks Rac1 accumulation.

claim: Inhibition of endocytosis in soft-gel cultures for 1 hr significantly increased manifestation of the broad lamellipodium phenotype at the 5 hr time-point.
source: In support of the idea that Rac1 accumulation requires endocytosis (Figure 2A), inhibition of endocytosis in soft-gel cultures for 1 hr also significantly increased manifestation of the BL phenotype at the 5 hr time-point (Figure 2C1), with >90% of cells exhibiting sparsely distributed and less activated Rac1 and broad lamellipodia that resembled those seen on 20 kPa gels (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological analysis of neurons treated with endocytosis inhibitors shown in Figure 2C1.

claim: The number of neurite-bearing neurons was decreased to ~13% following endocytosis inhibition compared to the untreated control.
source: The number of neurite-bearing neurons was also decreased to ~13% compared to the untreated control (Figure 2C2).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of neurite formation following endocytosis inhibition shown in Figure 2C2.

claim: Bath-application of Y27632 or the PI3k inhibitor LY294002 to 0.1 kPa cultures did not alter the onset of lamellipodial segmentation.
source: In contrast, bath-application of Y27632 (an inhibitor of Rho-associated protein kinase, ROCK) or the PI3k inhibitor LY294002 to 0.1 kPa cultures did not alter the onset of lamellipodial segmentation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that ROCK and PI3K inhibition do not affect lamellipodial segmentation.

claim: Cells grown on stiff substrates (20 kPa gels or glass) expressed higher levels of adhesion factors than endocytic factors.
source: In 5 hr cultures on stiff substrates (20 kPa gels or glass), cells expressed higher levels of adhesion factors (such as integrin β1; for the level of active integrin, please see Appendix 1—figure 3) than endocytic factors (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis of protein expression shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Cells grown on soft gels (0.1 kPa and 1 kPa) expressed higher levels of factors associated with clathrin-mediated endocytosis, including myosin VI, clathrin heavy chain and CIP4.
source: By contrast, cells grown on soft gels (0.1 kPa and 1 kPa) expressed higher levels of factors associated with clathrin-mediated endocytosis, including myosin VI, clathrin heavy chain (CHC) and Cdc42 interacting protein 4 (CIP4) (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis showing increased expression of endocytic factors on soft substrates.

claim: Expression levels of paxillin and phosphorylated paxillin in cultured neurons matched the profiles of endocytic factors rather than adhesion factors.
source: We observed that expression levels of paxillin and phosphorylated paxillin in cultured neurons did not match the profiles of other adhesion factors, but instead matched the profiles of endocytic factors (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis comparing protein expression patterns shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Cells grown on soft substrates (0.1 kPa gels) expressed significantly higher levels of paxillin than those grown on stiff substrates.
source: Further analysis of relative paxillin expression in 5 hr cultures indicated that cells grown on soft substrates (0.1 kPa gels) expressed significantly higher levels of paxillin than those grown on stiff substrates (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative Western blot analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: More than 30% of paxillin from brain lysates co-fractionated with the endocytosis factors Rab5 and CHC in floating membrane fractions.
source: We found >30% of paxillin from brain lysates co-fractionated with the endocytosis factors Rab5 and CHC (in floating membrane fractions), whereas co-fractionation was <5% in cardiac lysates (Figure 3—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane flotation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: A significant proportion (~39%) of paxillin staining colocalized with that of AAK1 rather than p-FAKY397 on soft gels (0.1 kPa).
source: A significant proportion (~39%) of paxillin staining colocalized with that of AAK1 rather than p-FAKY397 on soft gels (0.1 kPa; Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence colocalization analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In cells exhibiting a segmented lamellipodium phenotype on soft gels (0.1 kPa), a significant portion (>40%) of paxillin appeared in a punctate pattern and co-localized with the endocytic factors CHC or AAK1.
source: In cells exhibiting an SL phenotype on soft gels (0.1 kPa), enhanced resolution confocal microscopy also revealed that a significant portion (>40%) of paxillin appeared in a punctate pattern and co-localized with the endocytic factors CHC or AAK1 (Pearson's coefficient >0.75) rather than adhesion factors p-FAKY397 or vinculin (Pearson's coefficient <0.45) (Figure 3D,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by high-resolution confocal microscopy and colocalization analysis shown in Figures 3D and 3F.

claim: Paxillin preferentially associated with p-FAKY397 and vinculin in cells exhibiting broad lamellipodia on stiff gels (20 kPa).
source: Interestingly, paxillin preferentially associated with p-FAKY397 and vinculin in cells exhibiting BL on stiff gels (20 kPa; Figure 3E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization analysis on stiff substrates shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: LC-MS/MS analysis identified several endocytic factors that bind to paxillin, including clathrin, dynamin, and CIP4.
source: Our analyses identified several endocytic factors that bind to paxillin, including clathrin, dynamin, and CIP4 (Figure 4A–C, and Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis and co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figures 4A-C and Appendix 1—table 3.

claim: The binding affinity of paxillin to endocytic factors increased with substrate compliance, whereas the binding affinity of paxillin to vinculin increased with substrate stiffness.
source: Moreover, the binding affinity of paxillin to these factors increased with substrate compliance, whereas the binding affinity of paxillin to vinculin increased with substrate stiffness (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing substrate-dependent binding preferences shown in Figure 4A.

claim: GST-PXNFL associated with His-CIP4FL but not His-CIP4ΔF-BAR.
source: GST-PXNFL associated with His-CIP4FL but not His-CIP4ΔF-BAR (Figure 4B), confirming that the F-BAR domain is required for paxillin binding.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro GST pulldown assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Deletion of the LIM3-4 domain reduced paxillin affinity for vinculin and CIP4.
source: Furthermore, using an in vitro GST pulldown assay and domain mapping analysis in HEK293T cell lysates, we found that deletion of the LIM3-4 domain reduced paxillin affinity for vinculin and CIP4 (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by domain mapping experiments shown in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: Ectopic expression of full-length CIP4 or the F-BAR domain alone in HEK293T cells decreased association of both GST-PXNFL and endogenous paxillin with vinculin dose-dependently.
source: Indeed, ectopic expression of full-length CIP4 or the F-BAR domain alone in HEK293T cells decreased association of both GST-PXNFL (Figure 4E) and endogenous paxillin (Figure 4F) with vinculin dose-dependently, but ectopic expression of the F-BAR-deleted CIP4 mutant (ΔN'-F-BAR) did not (Figure 4F, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by competitive binding assays shown in Figures 4E, 4F, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: Reducing paxillin and CIP4 levels by shRNA significantly decreased the rate and level of FM4-64 uptake in neurons grown on soft gels (0.1 kPa).
source: Reducing paxillin and CIP4 levels in this way significantly decreased the rate and level of FM4-64 uptake (endocytosis) in neurons grown on soft gels (0.1 kPa; Figure 5A,C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM4-64 uptake assays in knockdown neurons shown in Figures 5A, 5C, and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ectopic expression of full-length paxillin potentiated FM4-64 uptake in neurons grown on both soft and stiff gels (0.1 kPa or 20 kPa).
source: Furthermore, ectopic expression of full-length paxillin potentiated FM4-64 uptake in neurons grown on both soft and stiff gels (0.1 kPa or 20 kPa; relative to untransfected neighboring control cells); an effect not seen following ectopic expression of paxillinΔLIM3-4 or paxillinLD1-3, which lacks the LIM-domain required for CIP4 association (Figure 5B,D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by FM4-64 uptake assays in neurons overexpressing paxillin variants shown in Figures 5B, 5D, and 5E.

claim: Co-transfection of paxillin shRNA C and shRNA D significantly reduced QD-BDNF internalization by approximately 8-fold.
source: Histograms showing that co-transfection of paxillin shRNA C and shRNA D significantly reduced QD-BDNF internalization (as reflected by an ~8-fold reduction in the quantity of intracellular QD-BDNF). Data represent means ±SEM (n ≥ 3 independent experiments, 26–52 cells for each set of experiments; compared to scrambled shRNA control; ***p<0.001; ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc test).
evidence: The claim is supported by QD-BDNF internalization assays in HEK293T cells shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Paxillin knockdown significantly increased the percentage of neurons exhibiting the broad lamellipodium morphology and reduced the number of neurons bearing neurites in 16 hr cultures on soft substrates (0.1 kPa).
source: On soft substrates (0.1 kPa), paxillin knockdown significantly increased the percentage of neurons exhibiting the BL morphology and reduced the number of neurons bearing neurites in 16 hr cultures, with these effects being similar to those seen following treatment with the endocytosis inhibitors (Figure 2B, and Figure 7A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological analysis of paxillin knockdown neurons shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: Paxillin knockdown significantly reduced levels of active Rac1 accumulation at the protruding edge.
source: Further, paxillin knockdown significantly reduced levels of active Rac1 accumulation at the protruding edge (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis of active Rac1 in paxillin knockdown neurons shown in Figures 7C and 7D.

claim: Ectopic PXN∆LIM3-4 expression in 0.1 kPa cultures enhanced the neuritogenesis-delaying broad lamellipodium phenotype.
source: Using this approach, we found that ectopic PXN∆LIM3-4 expression in 0.1 kPa cultures enhanced the neuritogenesis-delaying BL phenotype, whereas PXN∆LD1 expression reduced the BL population in 20 kPa cultures (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological analysis of neurons expressing paxillin deletion mutants shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: PXN∆LD1 expression reduced the broad lamellipodium population in 20 kPa cultures.
source: Using this approach, we found that ectopic PXN∆LIM3-4 expression in 0.1 kPa cultures enhanced the neuritogenesis-delaying BL phenotype, whereas PXN∆LD1 expression reduced the BL population in 20 kPa cultures (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological analysis of neurons expressing paxillin deletion mutants shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: High levels of endocytosis-related factors and low levels of adhesion-related molecules were observed in embryonic rat brains compared to hepatic and cardiac control tissues.
source: We observed high levels of endocytosis-related factors and low levels of adhesion-related molecules in embryonic rat brains compared to hepatic and cardiac control tissues (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis of tissue lysates shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Paxillin abundance increased between E13 and E18 and declined postnatally (between P1 and P14) in the developing cortex.
source: In addition, paxillin abundance increased between E13 and E18 and declined postnatally (between P1 and P14) in the developing cortex (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot analysis of brain lysates at different developmental stages shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: Neurons expressing paxillin-shRNA showed apparent migration defects relative to controls, with ~42% of cells accumulating in the subventricular zone.
source: Neurons expressing paxillin-shRNA showed apparent migration defects relative to controls, with ~42% of cells accumulating in the SVZ, wherein ~25% of paxillin-knockdown neurons did not exhibit neurite processes (Figure 7E,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo analysis of paxillin knockdown neurons shown in Figures 7E and 7G.

claim: Approximately 25% of paxillin-knockdown neurons did not exhibit neurite processes in the subventricular zone.
source: Neurons expressing paxillin-shRNA showed apparent migration defects relative to controls, with ~42% of cells accumulating in the SVZ, wherein ~25% of paxillin-knockdown neurons did not exhibit neurite processes (Figure 7E,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological analysis of paxillin knockdown neurons in vivo shown in Figures 7E and 7G.

claim: The phenotypes of paxillin knockdown were rescued by co-expression of shRNA-resistant PXN-R.
source: These phenotypes were rescued by co-expression of shRNA-resistant PXN-R (Figure 7E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiments shown in Figures 7E-G.

claim: Paxillin plays a dual role in adhesion and endocytosis, with predominance of one of these roles determining the fate of a newborn neuron.
source: What is striking is our finding that paxillin plays a dual role in adhesion and endocytosis, with predominance of one of these roles determining the fate of a newborn neuron.
evidence: The claim is a summary interpretation of the experimental findings presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: On soft gels in particular, newborn neurons recruit paxillin to the endocytic machinery (via binding with clathrin and CIP4) with a higher, but not exclusive, preference over cell-matrix adhesions.
source: Our findings suggest that on soft gels in particular, newborn neurons recruit paxillin to the endocytic machinery (via binding with clathrin and CIP4) with a higher, but not exclusive, preference over cell-matrix adhesions.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on the binding affinity and colocalization data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A soft environment with elasticity lower than 1 kPa is sufficient to induce timely neurite initiation.
source: As a result, a soft environment with elasticity lower than 1 kPa is sufficient to induce timely neurite initiation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations on neurite formation on different substrate stiffnesses.

claim: Culturing cells on rigid substrates, disruption of Rac1 activation, and blockage of endocytosis all delay spontaneous neurite initiation.
source: Conversely, our observations suggest that culturing cells on rigid substrates, disruption of Rac1 activation, and blockage of endocytosis all delay spontaneous neurite initiation.
evidence: The claim is a summary of experimental observations showing delayed neurite initiation under various conditions.

claim: The ability of neonatal neurons to delay neuritogenesis on a rigid environment could endow cells with the ability to establish robust and functional networks only in permissive environments.
source: The ability of neonatal neurons to delay neuritogenesis on a rigid environment could endow cells with the ability to establish robust and functional networks only in permissive environments (i.e. soft microenvironments).
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the observed phenomena.

claim: Paxillin-associated endocytosis may also occur in epithelial cells, since both epithelial cells and neurons are derived from ectoderm.
source: Paxillin-associated endocytosis may also occur in epithelial cells, since both epithelial cells and neurons are derived from ectoderm.
evidence: The claim is a speculative extension based on developmental lineage relationships.

claim: A neuronal switch favoring paxillin/endocytic factor binding is required and activated immediately after embryonic neuronal differentiation to ensure timely neurite initiation.
source: Based on studies reporting the natural stiffness of mouse embryonic cerebral cortex at E16.5 to E18.5 (Iwashita et al., 2014), we surmise that a neuronal switch favoring paxillin/endocytic factor binding is required and activated immediately after embryonic neuronal differentiation to ensure timely neurite initiation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental findings and cited literature on brain stiffness.

claim: At a later developmental time-point and at synaptic contact sites, the paxillin adhesion switch may predominate, allowing contacts with postsynaptic cells or decreasing the capacity for neurite outgrowth.
source: However, at a later developmental time-point (since brain stiffness increases with age) and at synaptic contact sites, the paxillin adhesion switch may predominate, allowing contacts with postsynaptic cells or decreasing the capacity for neurite outgrowth.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation about the role of paxillin at later developmental stages.

claim: Besides substrate stiffness, physiological constraints imposed by other factors, such as cell-cell contact guidance or actin-microtubule coupling efficiency, could play important roles in neurite formation.
source: Besides substrate stiffness, physiological constraints imposed by other factors, such as cell-cell contact guidance or actin-microtubule coupling efficiency, could play important roles in neurite formation.
evidence: The claim acknowledges additional factors that may influence neurite formation beyond those studied.

claim: Paxillin-associated endocytosis may also potentiate retrograde relay of growth and survival signals deployed from the neuritic terminal.
source: In addition to a morphogenetic role, paxillin-associated endocytosis may also potentiate retrograde relay of growth and survival signals deployed from the neuritic terminal (Cosker and Segal, 2014) and thereby provide another mechanism to positively regulate neuronal development.
evidence: The claim is a speculative extension of the findings, citing literature on retrograde signaling.

claim: Polyacrylamide gels with elastic moduli of 0.1, 1, and 20 kPa were engineered and verified by atomic force microscopy.
source: Gels of three elastic moduli—0.1, 1 and 20 kPa—were engineered and verified by atomic force microscopy (see Materials and methods, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the methods description and AFM measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: Surface laminin was detectable on 0.1 kPa, 20 kPa and glass surfaces, and it was comparable following 5 and 16 hr incubation periods in neuronal culture media.
source: Moreover, surface laminin was detectable on 0.1 kPa, 20 kPa and glass surfaces, and it was comparable following 5 and 16 hr incubation periods in neuronal culture media (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), ruling out a difference due to coating.
evidence: The claim is supported by laminin immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The natural stiffness of brain tissue is E = 0.1–1 kPa.
source: By contrast, newborn neurons, which naturally reside in extremely soft tissue environments (E = 0.1–1 kPa) such as brain (Christ et al., 2010; Georges et al., 2006), behave differently.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to literature reporting brain tissue stiffness measurements.

claim: Soft mechanical properties generally favor neuronal differentiation and maturation.
source: Soft mechanical properties generally favor neuronal differentiation (Engler et al., 2006; Saha et al., 2008) and maturation (Balgude et al., 2001; Fawcett et al., 1995; Leach et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Neurons extend long protrusions known as neurites toward softer surfaces when cultured on substrates showing a stiffness gradient.
source: In particular, neurons extend long protrusions known as neurites toward softer surfaces when cultured on substrates showing a stiffness gradient (Sundararaghavan et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study on durotaxis.

claim: Retinal ganglion cells of Xenopus embryos exhibited a noticeable pattern of stiffness gradients within the optic tracts toward their targets in the optic tectum.
source: In vivo evidence for the inverse durotaxis of neuronal cells has been provided recently using retinal ganglion cells of Xenopus embryos, which exhibited a noticeable pattern of stiffness gradients within the optic tracts toward their targets in the optic tectum (Koser et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a study providing in vivo evidence of inverse durotaxis.

claim: Endocytosis is required to activate and recruit the neuritogenic signal molecule Rac1 to the membrane.
source: Furthermore, endocytosis is required to activate and recruit the neuritogenic signal molecule Rac1 (Palamidessi et al., 2008) to the membrane, an activity that enhances formation of cell protrusions through actin filament polymerization (Hall, 1998; McMahon and Boucrot, 2011; Merrifield and Kaksonen, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies on endocytosis and Rac1 activation.

claim: Paxillin is an adaptor protein composed of N-terminal LD motifs and C-terminal LIM domains.
source: Structurally, paxillin is an adaptor protein composed of N-terminal LD motifs and C-terminal LIM domains, both of which are important for binding to focal adhesion factors (Brown et al., 1996; Brown et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations describing paxillin structure.

claim: Vinculin exhibits a well-characterized paxillin-binding subdomain or 'PBS'.
source: Among those factors, vinculin exhibits a well-characterized paxillin-binding subdomain or 'PBS' (Tachibana et al., 1995; Wood et al., 1994).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies characterizing the vinculin-paxillin interaction.

claim: CIP4 dimerizes in vitro and in vivo via its F-BAR domain.
